newsitem.title: UK: Pearson names new senior officers.
newsitem.headline: Pearson names new senior officers.

text.p: British media group Pearson Plc said on Thursday that Marjorie Scardino and Dennis Stevenson will take over as chief executive and chairman of the group respectively. Scardino, currently chief executive of The Economist Group, which is 50 percent owned by Pearson, succeeds Frank Barlow at the end of the year.

Stevenson, who is a non-executive director, becomes deputy chairman with immediate effect, taking over from Michael Blakenham as chairman at Pearson's annual meeting in May, 1997. Blakenham said in statement, "These appointments complete the succession process at Pearson...I believe she (Scardino) will make a great contribution to the continuing evolution of the group's business." Blakenham has been chairman of Pearson since 1983 following a six year stint as chief executive.

Barlow, who has been chief executive for seven years, had agreed to extend his contract for a further two years after his retirement date in 1995, in order to help implement the group's strategy to focus on the media sector.
"I think Pearson's future is very favourable and Marjorie Scardino is a very good appointment," Barlow told Reuters.
Pearson interests include television and the Financial Times newspaper.

Scardino has been chief executive of the Economist since 1992, before which she headed its North American operations. Prior to that, she was partner in a Savannah, Georgia law firm and publisher and founder, with her husband, of the Pulitzer Prize-winning newspaper the Georgia Gazette.
Stevenson is chairman of aircraft leasing group GPA and is also a non-executive director of British Sky Broadcasting, J. Rothschild Assurance Plc and Manpower Inc.
